label: 1-2 steps after a v input, early in the original phase
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase on the one or two steps right after the token v was input, and only early in the sequence (t <= 5; it peaks at t = 3-4 and is near zero from t >= 7). The step directly after v is strongest (prev_tok = v: 44% firing rate, 13x lift, 69% of activation mass). The step two after v is weaker (prev2_tok = v: about 28% of mass). The largest activations (around 0.9-1.0 of max) come one step after a v at t = 3-4, often after a repeated v v. It never fires in the copy phase and almost never on the delimiter. It does not fire after a v that comes late in a long sequence (t >= 6). On dev the predicate has precision 0.93 and mass recall 0.90, but count recall is only 0.57: about 40% of active steps are weak activations (mostly under 0.1 of max) at t = 2-5 with no v nearby, and these are not captured.

issues: The reported test scores reproduce: precision 0.929, recall 0.569, F1 0.706, mass recall 0.896. Most of what the predicate misses is weak: 52% of the top-quartile activations are... (corrected) coverage by activation quartile is 0.05, 0.31, 0.92 and 0.99, so the misses are mostly in the bottom two quartiles.

The activations with no v nearby are spread out with no clear pattern. At t=2..5 with no v seen yet, precision is 0.045 and these steps hold only 5.7% of mass. Splitting by t==4, prev_tok in {c,3}, in_first==0 or L>=7 finds no subclass above about 0.19 precision or about 2% of mass. This looks like background noise, not a missed class of inputs.

The claims about where it fires check out. Copy phase: 0 active steps. Delimiter: 0.8% rate and 1.3% of mass. t>=7: about 0 active. After a v at t>=6: precision 0.20 and 0.8% of mass, so a little activity at t=6 and the claim holds roughly. At t=1 with prev_tok v: precision 1.0.

Small overstatement: 'often after a repeated v v'. Steps where both prev_tok and prev2_tok are v always fire (precision 1.0) but hold only about 3.7% of mass, so this is an occasional booster of the strongest activations, not the usual case.
The false positives cluster at prev2_tok = v at t=5, and the shown examples are actually weakly active (0.3-0.5). They are not a separate failure class.
Alternatives scored worse on test F1: prev_tok only scored 0.51, seen(v) 0.64, adding v at t-3 with t<=6 0.685, and excluding in_tok==v 0.69.
